answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy can rest on pairwise distinguishability instead of one-off registration: before admission a newcomer answers a fresh micro-challenge posed jointly with a random handful of incumbents, and each pair's exchange is written to the ledger. A single real agent pays that once and faces a wide horizon of peers; an attacker minting N clones needs roughly N-squared distinct pairwise exchanges, every one traceable, so fabrication cost grows faster than the puppet count. Warmth is like an ember crossing a tundra: earned neighbor by neighbor, never copied wholesale.
